resolutions.researcher_notes: Both sources confirm the project was actively under FERC review with a firm completion target of 2Q 2019 (FERC's Aug 2017 Notice of Schedule sets the EA completion date and describes the certificated facilities; Pipeline & Gas Journal's Oct 2018 'Planned Projects' entry for the Stratton Ridge Project lists 'Completion: 2Q 2019'), consistent with Status=operating today. Neither source directly states a post-2019 in-service confirmation, so this is a same-generation (FERC docket + trade press reporting on that docket) pairing rather than two fully independent confirmations of actual completion -- set medium/not-independent. Did not find a dedicated post-2019 'now in service' announcement (WhiteWater/Enbridge's own project page for this line is a 404 live and its only Wayback capture, Sep 2017, predates completion; searched EIA pipeline projects data and NGI/RBN trade press with no dedicated Stratton Ridge in-service story surfacing).

FERC's Feb 2017 Notice of Application (Docket CP17-56/CP17-57): the project 'will create 322,000 Dth/d of firm transportation capacity to deliver natural gas' -- filed under Natural Gas Act section 7(c), i.e. a gas pipeline. Pipeline & Gas Journal's Mar 2018 'Planned Projects' entry independently lists the Stratton Ridge Project under its natural-gas pipeline planned-projects table with 'Capacity: 322 MDth/d.' Two distinct publishers (federal regulator + trade press) agreeing this is a natural gas facility.

Enbridge's own project page (live URL now 404s; content confirmed via its Sep 2017 Wayback capture, fetched directly with curl since the site is enbridge.com's legacy CMS, not a JS shell): 'anticipated to be in service the first quarter of 2019' / 'expected in-service date: First half 2019.' Pipeline & Gas Journal's Oct 2018 'Planned Projects' entry, filed roughly a year later and independent of Enbridge, lists 'Completion: 2Q 2019' for the same FERC docket (CP17-57). Both distinct publishers point to a 2019 in-service year, matching StartYear1=2019 (the two figures differ by a quarter -- Q1 per Enbridge's earlier estimate vs Q2 per PGJ's later trade-press figure -- which is normal schedule slippage between a project's initial estimate and an updated trade-press report, not a contradiction of the YEAR).

FERC's Feb 2017 Notice of Application: 'The Project will create 322,000 Dth/d of firm transportation capacity' (322,000 Dth/d = 322 MMcf/d, standard prose/unit equivalence). Pipeline & Gas Journal's Mar 2018 'Planned Projects' table entry for the Stratton Ridge Project independently lists 'Capacity: 322 MDth/d' (MDth/d = thousand Dth/d = same figure). Two distinct publishers (federal regulator + trade press) agreeing on 322,000 Dth/d / 322 MMcf/d. Note the S&P Global Market Intelligence seed citation's own headline ('Texas Eastern applies for 322,000-Dth/d Stratton Ridge expansion project') also states this figure, but its article body is paywalled/lead-gated even via its Dec 2021/Jan 2022 Wayback capture (only the headline text is served; a 'Request a Demo' form fills the rest), so it was not used as a proposed ref though its headline is consistent.

FERC's Aug 2017 Notice of Schedule for Environmental Review states the Project Description in full: it 'would consist of: A new Angleton Compressor Station ... a new 0.5 mile, 30-inch-diameter pipeline lateral in Brazoria County, Texas to interconnect with the BIG intrastate pipeline system ...' -- an exact match to LengthKnown=0.50 mi. This is the only source found stating a specific mileage figure (Enbridge's own page and both PGJ entries describe the project by capacity/cost/counties but give no length figure, and PGJ's Mar 2018 issue's 'West Columbia, TX - Stratton Ridge, TX' / 320 MDth/d entry is a DIFFERENT, similarly-named project -- the 'SK Pipeline' supporting the same Freeport Train III expansion, not this one, so it was not used here to avoid conflating two projects). Single-source corroboration only -- medium/not independent.

Searched the FERC docket (Notice of Application, Notice of Schedule, Federal Register listing), Enbridge's own 2017 project page, and both PGJ 'Planned Projects' entries. All of them describe the constructed facilities (Angleton Compressor Station, the 0.5-mile lateral, and modifications at Mont Belvieu and other stations) as located entirely in Texas (Brazoria, Chambers, San Jacinto, Lavaca, Waller and Shelby counties), with the FERC application describing the capacity as sourced from 'multiple receipt points on Texas Eastern's interstate pipeline system' without naming Louisiana specifically. Texas Eastern Transmission's mainline is broadly known to run from the Gulf Coast (Texas/Louisiana) to the Northeast (confirmed via Wikipedia's Enbridge article: TETCo 'transport[s] gas from the Gulf of Mexico coast in Texas to the New York City area'), which is consistent with but does not confirm a Louisiana receipt point for this specific capacity lease. No source found that explicitly names a Louisiana location for this project -- ruling out a citation here rather than proposing an inferred one; not flagged as a CONCERN since TETCO's system legitimately spans into Louisiana and the sheet's Start=Louisiana/End=Texas is plausible, just not corroborated by anything found.

Enbridge's own project page states: 'The Stratton Ridge Project, including the BIG Pipeline acquisition, has an expected capital expenditure of approximately $200 million' -- an exact match to SegmentCost=200,000,000 USD. Single-source only: Pipeline & Gas Journal's Mar 2018 entry for the same docket (CP17-57) instead lists 'Cost: $94 million' -- this is NOT a contradiction of the sheet value but a narrower figure (the $94M appears to be the incremental construction/facilities cost alone, excluding the roughly $106M BIG Pipeline acquisition-and-lease component that Enbridge's own $200M figure explicitly includes: 'including the BIG Pipeline acquisition'). Proposed only the $200M source since it matches the sheet's value on an apples-to-apples basis; the PGJ $94M figure was deliberately NOT proposed here to avoid citing a ref that does not support the stated value, but is noted below.
CONCERN: the sheet's SegmentCost=200,000,000 appears to be the total project cost (construction + BIG Pipeline acquisition/lease), not the incremental pipeline-construction cost alone (PGJ's independently reported $94 million) -- worth confirming which cost basis GEM intends for SegmentCost, since a future editor citing PGJ alone would see $94M and could 'correct' the cell incorrectly.

Enbridge Inc.'s FY2023 10-K, Exhibit 21.1 (List of Subsidiaries, filed with the SEC 2024-02-09) lists 'Texas Eastern Transmission, LP' as an Enbridge subsidiary -- confirms Owner1=Enbridge for the operator entity that owns and built this project (per the FERC docket, Texas Eastern Transmission, LP is the certificate holder). Wikipedia's Enbridge article independently corroborates the acquisition history: 'Spectra owned the Texas Eastern Pipeline (TETCo) ... The merger was completed on February[27, 2017].' This traces the ownership chain Spectra Energy Partners (100% owner per Enbridge's own 2017 project page) -> Enbridge (post-2017 merger, later fully absorbed via the 2018 Spectra Energy Partners buy-in) -> Owner1=Enbridge today. Two distinct publishers (an SEC-filed corporate document + Wikipedia, citable per this brief's rules as one secondary source) agreeing on the Enbridge/Texas Eastern relationship. Owner1%=100.00% was not independently found stated as a percentage anywhere, but is consistent with Texas Eastern Transmission being a wholly owned, consolidated subsidiary per the Exhibit 21.1 listing style (no minority-interest caveat given).
